We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.

title: CoLink: Global Compression and Knowledge Linking for Multi-Turn Dialogue Modeling
summary: Extracting salient information from long-horizon dialogue histories remains a significant challenge for Large Language Models (LLMs) due to the restricted context windows and efficient retrieval challenges. Current methods typically rely on history organization or local token-level optimization, suffering from information loss, retrieval redundancy, and myopic attention. Inspired by the view in cognitive science that dialogue constitutes sense-making and memory association, we propose CoLink, a framework that enhances LLMs' global context awareness in domain-specific multi-turn dialogues through information linking and compression. CoLink first clusters historical contexts into topic graphs to establish cross-semantic associations with external knowledge. Guided by the adaptive control of thought, it then retrieves and activates knowledge via synergizing semantic relevance and graph-structural topology. Crucially, to achieve effective compression of history and knowledge, we ground multi-turn dialogues in information theory and derive a principled optimization objective for extracting the core sense-making information. Coupled with a competitive slot mechanism, CoLink condenses the global context into dedicated memory and knowledge slots, efficiently distilling lengthy, redundant inputs into an extremely compact latent representation. Extensive empirical results on both public and our MMD datasets validate CoLink's superiority and generalizability in knowledge linking and sense modeling.

title: CrossPair: Unlocking Generalist Visual Transformation Learning in Image Editors
summary: Language models switch tasks from demonstrations, but vision still often relies on separate systems for restoration, editing, and stylization. A before--after example offers a shared instruction only if the transferable change can be separated from the scene that demonstrates it. We introduce CrossPair, which adapts a pretrained multimodal image editor to transfer diverse transformations from one exemplar pair. Exemplar-before, exemplar-after, and query images take fixed roles in its native VLM and VAE pathways: the VLM extracts operation semantics, while the VAE retains fine appearance and structure. A training-only, change-aware DINOv3 objective aligns feature-change directions across content-distinct scenes, guiding the output to follow the demonstrated relation without an inference-time encoder. We construct Transform-360K by grouping filtered pairs from conditional representations, restoration, editing, virtual try-on, and stylization under shared transformations. On Relation252K-derived seen and held-out transformations, \method improves target agreement and edit-direction similarity over released systems. Ablations show that the semantic and visual exemplar routes are complementary and that DINO relation alignment further strengthens transfer; Transform-360K training also improves aggregate held-out-operation scores.

title: Finite-Distance Imaging of Relativistic Equilibrium Tori around Genuine Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson Black Holes
summary: We calculate finite-distance images of stationary, pressure-supported tori around genuine, electrically neutral Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson black holes using general relativistic ray tracing with gray emission and absorption. The emitting volume is bounded by a constant-specific-angular-momentum equilibrium free surface, and the observer is placed at a radius of $50M$. Along the investigated external-field sequence, integrated brightness and apparent size both increase strongly as the field modifies the equilibrium source and photon propagation. Higher torus filling has a different effect: in a representative sequence, brightness grows by a factor of $5.9$ while the intensity-weighted image size increases by only $10\%$. Increasing viewing inclination enhances lateral brightness contrast. Stronger self-absorption can coexist with higher absolute brightness because emission and absorption scale together in the adopted gray prescription. At common pressure center and filling, increasing the dimensionless spin from $0.5$ to $0.95$ dims the retrograde sequence by a factor of about $7$ as its equilibrium contracts, whereas prograde brightness changes by only $2\%$. These contrasting responses show how the equilibrium boundary, fluid motion, and optical depth jointly shape the brightness, scale, and asymmetry of finite-distance torus images.

title: SHIFT-JEV: Certified Abstention and Gain-Gated Continual Adaptation for LLM-Based Decision Models under Distribution Shift
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can act as decision models that return a probability distribution over a fixed set of options, but deployed decision models face domain, label-prior, emerging-class and candidate-set shift. We study how such models fail under shift and propose SHIFT-Jev, a monitoring, abstention and continual-adaptation procedure for them. It scores the risk of each decision from uncertainty, format and option-consistency signals, certifies abstention thresholds with Learn-then-Test, monitors the decision stream with drift and label-shift detectors, and accepts a model update only when an expected-gain gate finds a significant held-out improvement without loss on earlier regimes. On a benchmark of ten shifted test environments with Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-4B (three seeds each) and Phi-4-mini, fine-tuning with KL anchors and temperature scaling lowers calibration error under shift from 0.289 to 0.087. At a target risk of 10%, a learned uncertainty score with a certified threshold exceeds the target in 3 to 5 of 27 environment-seed tests, against 5 to 15 for a max-probability score with the same certification and 9 to 14 for conformal prediction sets; drift-based routing changes little. A chi-squared test on predicted labels detects 95 to 99% of class-prior shifts that confidence- and embedding-based detectors miss. In continual adaptation, SHIFT-Jev reaches 70.5% accuracy on Qwen3-0.6B, above replay, LwF, EWC and fine-tuning baselines in every seed, whereas on Qwen3-4B its conservative gate leaves it 0.4 to 1.4 points behind them.

title: Universal Scaling of the Little-Parks Oscillation Amplitude
summary: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.

title: Developer Task Delegation to LLMs and the Trust Factor: A Mixed Methods Study
summary: With the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs), software developers are presented with a powerful new approach: delegating software development tasks to LLMs. Existing studies have explored task delegation for a subset of tasks and factors. Critically, what tasks developers delegate to LLMs, to what extent, and why they delegate them, is not yet well understood. We explore these questions through 22 interviews and a survey with 160 software practitioners. Developers reported employing four modes of task delegation to LLMs: full delegation, partial delegation, self-delegation, and task avoidance. Drawing on our qualitative findings, we discuss the rationales behind these choices and explore how task difficulty, task risk, developer motivation, and trust appear to be associated with software development task delegation to LLMs. Our statistical analysis reveals that trust is a significant factor associated with task delegation to LLMs. Finally, we share actionable implications for human-AI collaboration in software research, and for software practitioners to make the most of their newly found powers of delegation.

title: From Data Footprints to Researcher Fingerprints: Temporal Ego-centric Research Group Detection in Scientific Knowledge Graphs
summary: Understanding who researchers collaborate with, when and how their research groups form, and how these evolve over time is a foundational prerequisite for constructing multidimensional, evidence-based researcher fingerprints -- a requirement that has become increasingly urgent in the context of ongoing reforms in research evaluation advocated by initiatives such as DORA, the Leiden Manifesto, and CoARA. In this paper, we propose an egocentric approach for fine-grained research group detection, operating at the scale of individual researchers' ego networks, as extracted from Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SKGs), and requiring the ego node to be present in all identified research groups -- a constraint that is not merely technical but reflects a commitment to researcher-centred analysis. Our approach builds on the Leiden algorithm as its computational core and is grounded in SKGs, which provide the heterogeneous, open scholarly metadata necessary to trace collaboration patterns at scale in a reproducible and transparent manner. We evaluate the proposed method through a user evaluation involving 10 researchers with diverse backgrounds and career stages, demonstrating its ability to surface meaningful and interpretable collaboration structures. The research groups identified constitute the structural scaffold upon which richer characterisations of scholarly identity -- including roles, seniority, contribution types, and publication patterns -- can be built in subsequent work, contributing to the broader goal of fairer and more transparent research assessment.

title: Search for the rare decay $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$
summary: Using a data sample of $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^{6} J/ψ$ events collected with the BESIII detector, we search for the rare decay $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$ via the process $J/ψ\toγη^{\prime}$. No significant signal is observed and an upper limit on the branching fraction of $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$ is set at $\mathcal{B}(η^{\prime}\to 3γ) < 2.25\times 10^{-5}$ at the 90\% confidence level. This result improves the previous upper limit by more than a factor of four.

title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
summary: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincaré class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.

title: Factual Yet One-Sided: Stance Poisoning and Evidence Balancing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary:
The stance expressed in responses from retrieval-augmented generation systems is significantly influenced by the stance distribution of the retrieved materials. Existing research on knowledge poisoning has primarily targeted factual errors. In contrast, this study focuses on injection attacks in which the facts are correct but the stance on a controversial issue is one-sided. At a mean topic-level poisoning share of 18.9% within the post-injection ProCon documents, all four generation models from different vendors exhibited stance shifts aligned with the poisoning direction; across four concentration levels, the shifts increased monotonically.
  This paper proposes a Stance-Balancing Middleware positioned between the retriever and the generator. It consists of stance detection, fixed balancing (2 supporting + 2 opposing + 1 neutral), and a debiasing prompt, without introducing additional large language model calls. Across all eight concentration-direction settings, the complete method reduced the magnitude of stance deviation by an estimated 0.106 to 0.350; the six settings at poisoning shares of 11.9%-18.9% remained significant after Holm adjustment (adjusted p <= 0.009). In the cross-model experiment, all eight model-direction combinations moved along the stance axis in the corrective direction, and seven of eight showed a clearly detected reduction in absolute distance from 0. In the concentration sweep, the post-defense intervals included 0 in all eight settings, while the cross-model pro-poisoning results retained small positive residual point estimates of +0.045 to +0.063. For 20 candidate documents, stance detection took approximately 1.5% of the median generation time on a single GPU and approximately 16% on CPU.

title: Repairing Broken Access Control in Web Applications with LLMs: An Empirical Benchmark Study
summary: Broken access control (BAC) ranks among the most severe web-application vulnerability classes, yet its automated repair remains largely unexplored. Unlike memory-safety vulnerabilities, BAC is a logic vulnerability whose repair demands a deep understanding of an application's access-control model and business semantics, which traditional automated vulnerability repair techniques handle poorly. Large language models (LLMs) open a promising avenue for this problem, but no standard benchmark exists for studying how well they repair BAC vulnerabilities. We construct BAC-Bench, the first benchmark for BAC repair, consisting of 46 real-world BAC vulnerabilities drawn from six widely used web applications spanning four programming languages. Each vulnerability is equipped with a sandboxed runtime environment, a PoC validation program and a functional test program. We further propose a BAC repair-strategy framework that characterizes any BAC patch along four dimensions, Position, Coverage, Mechanism, and Content. Evaluating eight base LLMs and two commercial LLM agents on BAC-Bench, we find that single-turn base LLMs repair 37.68% of the vulnerabilities on average, while two minimal scaffolds, Apply-Feedback and Navigate-and-Locate, raise this average to 66.03%, with the best base LLM reaching 75.36%, close to the 78.99% of the best agent. Notably, some LLM-generated patches surpass the official patches, and one incidentally closed a zero-day vulnerability that had lain dormant for three years. Our findings delineate the current capability boundary of LLM-based BAC repair and offer guidance toward its practical adoption.

title: Synergizing Wireless Foundation Models and LLMs: A Multi-Task Framework for MA Systems
summary: While movable antennas (MAs) provide enhanced spatial flexibility through dynamic repositioning, they confront critical challenges in acquiring complete channel state information (CSI) and efficiently optimizing antenna positions. Encouragingly, wireless foundation models (WFMs) capture generalizable channel priors for high-quality CSI extrapolation, while large language models (LLMs) enable parameter-efficient, token-level optimization for wireless tasks. In this paper, we synergistically integrate a WFM and an LLM into a multi-task framework for MA systems. First, to address the mismatch between existing WFM pre-training and MA channel characteristics, we develop an MA-oriented ``ExtLWM'' based on the large wireless model (LWM) architecture. Second, we design a unified ExtLWM-Connector-LLM architecture that flexibly adapts to different MA configurations without structural redesign. Third, we reformulate discrete MA positioning as a sequential decision-making problem, where candidate positions are represented by numerical tokens and optimized using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to exploit the serial generation capability of the LLM. Finally, a multi-stage training strategy is developed to maintain multi-task performance under limited training samples while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results show that ExtLWM can produce high-quality channel embeddings while outperforming various benchmarks in CSI extrapolation. Meanwhile, the proposed LLM-based approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and computational complexity.

title: Recovering fractal boundary dimensions from Robin eigenvalues
summary: We study Robin problems in which a small local boundary coefficient competes with the increasing surface measure of a finite-depth fractal approximation. For a fixed smooth domain, layer potentials give Green function and eigenpair expansions; contour residues and a finite-rank reduction yield a quantitative spectral-gap-dependent eigenvalue remainder. For varying Lipschitz domains, a uniform Poincaré inequality and a trace estimate with respect to normalized surface measure give a uniform ground-state expansion and a rank-one resolvent singularity as the total Robin boundary mass tends to zero. Under the boundary-resolution hypothesis and the condition on the approximation scales, ground-state measurements with known Robin coefficients recover the lower and upper Minkowski dimensions for sequences with bounded total Robin boundary mass. We describe Neumann, generalized Robin, and Dirichlet-type operator limits under the corresponding compact Mosco convergence hypotheses. Koch snowflake computations illustrate the reconstruction formulas, and an exact finite-stage area correction improves the adjacent-stage dimension estimator.

title: Transformer to GPT-5: Advancements, Limitations, and Future Directions in Large Language Model Design
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized Artificial Intelligence (AI) by their extraordinary capabilities, like contextual understanding, few-shot/zero-shot learning, code generation, ability to reason and problem-solving. Recent studies have shown immense work on LLMs. Yet, there is limited work on the thorough taxonomy of LLMs. This study would showcase a detailed classification of LLMs, starting with the earlier models like BERT and leading to LLMs like GPT, Gemini, Claude and Grok. We would delve into topics like datasets used to train LLMs, computational power used during training, their hardware specifications, architecture and parameters. Further, we would also look at the limitations, computational challenges and open problems as well. This study would primarily focus on the timeline of LLMs, signifying their growth over the period. Findings reveal a clear pattern: models that optimize the ratio between architectural complexity and data quality exhibit stronger reasoning stability and better alignment, without proportionally increasing the computational load. This desired balance between scaling and sustainability is the defining characteristic of the current generation of AI.

title: A Russian, a Brazilian, and a German Walk into a Bar, Ask the Same Question-- And Get Three Different Answers: Profiling LLM Perspective Diversity on Contested Topics
summary: Large Language Models(LLMs) have shown strong performance on tasks with verifiable answers, but many real-world queries involve subjectivity, disagreement, and conflicting evidence. Most existing benchmarks for such queries remain English-centric, overlooking the vast diversity of perspectives held by users worldwide. To systematically study how LLM perspectives vary across languages, we curate PerspectivesQA, a manually verified multilingual dataset of globally contested topics covering 18 languages, and propose ROOTS, a framework that profiles linguistic, perspective, and framing diversity. We evaluate a diverse set of eight models covering both open-source and proprietary families at varying scales, establishing that LLMs hedge their answers in English but commit to positions in lower-resource languages. Larger models maintain a more consistent cross-lingual worldview, while smaller models are more easily swayed. All models also exhibit high sensitivity to minor surface-level input variations, producing notable stance even in larger models.

title: DoubleFree:Exploiting Exploration History for Rollout-Free Multi-Task LLMs Training
summary: Multi-task post-training can develop domain specialists through independent reinforcement learning (RL) and consolidate their capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). However, standard MOPD generates on-policy student responses and keeps multiple teachers online throughout consolidation, introducing substantial system costs. We view this pipeline as domain-wise exploration followed by cross-domain exploitation. Domain RL produces not only the final specialists, but also the trajectories collected throughout their training. Existing methods primarily use the former while leaving the latter underutilized. We introduce DoubleFree, which reuses these historical trajectories for rollout-free consolidation and precomputes teacher supervision for online-teacher-free student training. To understand why this works, we analyze when updates from historical trajectories can approximate on-policy distillation updates and how combining trajectories across exploration stages can better support an evolving student. DoubleFree requires only minimal changes to existing post-training frameworks. Across math, code, and instruction following on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and SmolLM3-3B, DoubleFree achieves $2.99$-$5.75\times$ consolidation speedups and reduces GPU-hours by $80.9$-$90.1\%$, while maintaining comparable multi-domain performance.

title: Andreev Reflection at a Graphene Normal-Superconductor Interface: A Lattice-Continuum Comparison
summary:
We compare quadratic continuum and nearest-neighbour tight-binding models of Andreev reflection at a clean graphene normal-superconductor interface. For abrupt changes in chemical potential and pairing potential, with unchanged hopping, the lattice model yields four independent boundary conditions. Its reflection probabilities agree with independent Kwant calculations to numerical precision for the channels examined.
  We investigate trigonal warping and its effect on the relation between momentum and group velocity. For $(μ_N,μ_S,Δ_0,E)/t_0=(0.5,1,0.1,0.05)$, the Andreev-reflection probability for the $ξ=+1$ valley peaks at $19.9^\circ$ in the lattice model, versus $3.4^\circ$ in the quadratic continuum model. These parameters lie outside the expected validity regime of the low-energy approximation. As all energy scales are reduced at fixed ratios, the central angular response and conductance become more consistent with lattice results.
  The quadratic continuum boundary problem also requires short-wavelength auxiliary modes outside the validity range of the valley expansion. Thus, differences cannot be attributed to bulk dispersion alone. A small excitation energy relative to chemical potential does not ensure continuum validity; relevant energy scales, modes in both regions, and interface matching assumptions must also be considered.

title: All-plus Yang--Mills and gravity wavefunctions in de Sitter space
summary: We present sewing representations for tree-level all-plus wavefunctions in four-dimensional de Sitter space. For Yang--Mills theory, the arbitrary-multiplicity formula is a sum over noncrossing polygon dissections, with each cell carrying energy differences of a full lower-point wavefunction. The absence of a generic total-energy pole is manifest, while partial-energy residues are determined by the lower-point factors. We derive this representation from self-dual Yang--Mills solutions. For Einstein gravity, we propose an arbitrary-multiplicity formula consisting of an alternating sum over labelled sewing trees plus a local gravitational Chern--Simons term. This local term arises from the self-dual Einstein action and supplies boundary data not fixed by internal-energy cuts. We derive a generating formula for it from the boundary connection and give explicit expressions through seven points.

title: MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts
summary: Skill documents are becoming the default adaptation surface for frozen large language model (LLM) agents, but current skill generators face two key limitations. First, humans and different LLMs differ in how they organize procedural knowledge and approach task solving. Skills authored from a human or single-model perspective may therefore fail to align with the reasoning behaviors of other backbones, limiting cross-model generalization. Second, sequential skill descriptions inadequately represent procedures with parallel branches and explicit dependencies, while existing skill optimizers primarily operate on prose and lack explicit support for graph-structured skill evolution. We introduce MultiEvoSkill, a skill-optimization framework comprising three core components: 1) Skill compiler casts the skill as a typed graph with tailored operators, producing a compact, informative representation with explicit procedural topology; 2) Heterogeneous agent system proposes revision advices using collective intelligence, where minimal and informative issues are identified based on multiple sets of experiences. 3) Structure-aware debate and evolution mechanism organizes candidate edits into a heterogeneous graph, resolves them under dependency and importance constraints, and distills the collective proposal into the artifact. Multi-dimensional gating ensures the information gain and topological correctness of each evolution. Optimal skills are then obtained when the system converges at a consistent state. Various experiments and ablations against SOTA methods validate the effectiveness and generalization of MultiEvoSkill.

title: Recovering Business Rules as Cascade Lookups for Enterprise Field Prediction
summary: Enterprise sales-order systems rely on manually maintained configuration rules to determine fields such as payment terms, shipping points, and sales ownership. When these rules are incomplete or stale, operators must enter values by hand, and downstream errors spread into billing, logistics, and reporting. This paper studies whether missing or outdated rules can be recovered from historical transactions instead of being relearned as opaque statistical patterns. We introduce a knowledge-graph-guided workflow in which an LLM agent proposes candidate business keys, meaning column combinations such as customer and document type, validates them through SQL profiling, and compiles the resulting evidence into deterministic cascade lookups. The LLM is used only during offline rule discovery. At inference time, prediction is a transparent key lookup with no model-serving requirement. Experiments on enterprise sales-order prediction and public relational benchmarks show that cascades are most effective when fields follow stable business rules, while learned graph models remain preferable when prediction depends on temporal or neighborhood patterns. Drift analysis further turns residual errors into diagnostics for configuration maintenance. Code and data: https://github.com/Fireblossom/CascadER.

title: A marked scheme representation for Voronoi volumes in the Brownian map
summary: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.

title: A GPU-efficient local ADER finite-difference method for compressible-flow DNS
summary: Algorithm design tailored to graphics processing units (GPUs) can substantially improve the efficiency of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Efforts to adapt CFD solvers to GPUs often focus on spatial discretization, while time advancement commonly relies on multistage Runge--Kutta (RK) methods. However, these RK methods require repeated residual evaluations and full-domain operations, increasing the cost of compressible-flow direct numerical simulation (DNS). To reduce this overhead, we develop a local arbitrary high-order derivatives (ADER) finite-difference method that couples a compact ten-point quadratic predictor to a conservative central corrector through operator matching. With two quadrature nodes, one Picard correction, and selective dissipation, smooth convective tests recover third-order convergence under fixed-CFL refinement and near-seventh-order spatial behavior when background spatial error dominates. Temporal states remain kernel-local, and halo communication overlaps interior computation. Tests of smooth advection, periodic turbulence, and wall-bounded flows assess accuracy and flow statistics. On a $302^3$-node viscous Taylor--Green benchmark without heat conduction, throughput reaches 230.87 million node updates per second on one V100 GPU in double precision, 1.944 times that of spatially matched three-stage Runge--Kutta integration. Weak-scaling efficiency reaches 99.44\% from 4 to 32 V100 GPUs at 1.812 billion nodes.

title: Variational Cognitive Memory Abstraction for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable success in robotic manipulation, yet their ability to execute long-horizon tasks remains limited by insufficient long- term memory modeling. Existing methods either rely on implicit temporal representations within policy networks, where historical information can be gradually diluted, or maintain explicit memory buffers that suffer from redundancy, noise accumulation, and inefficient retrieval. In this paper, we propose CogMemory, a novel variational cognitive memory framework that enables VLA systems to selectively preserve and reuse task-relevant historical information. Our approach encodes multimodal trajectories into compact latent memory representations through a selective state- space memory encoder, multi-slot temporal abstraction, and variational information compression. During action generation, dynamic cross-attention retrieval with gated fusion adaptively incorporates relevant memories into policy prediction. With merely 3.45M additional parameters, CogMemory stays lightweight and seamlessly fits both early- and intermediate-fusion VLA backbones. Extensive experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse VLA backbones.

title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.2E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
summary: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. To our knowledge, this is the first intercity long distance frequency-ratio measurement, whose total uncertainty reaches the level required by the redefinition roadmap. The measured ratio exhibits a significant correlation with Earth tides and its response agree with the model within the statistical uncertainty. At intercity scale, this comparison demonstrates the capability of an optical-clock network for frequency comparison and Earths gravitational-potential sensing, a key step toward a wide-area optical-clock network.

title: HNSecW: A Logarithmic-Time MPC Protocol for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
summary: As a core component of modern RAG systems, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search has been extensively studied for decades. In practice, deploying ANN often requires symmetric privacy, where the querier's query and the database owner's data must remain hidden from each other, necessitating a secure multi-party computation (MPC) solution. So far, most MPC-based ANN protocols follow a cluster-based approach: they evaluate distances for the query over a large candidate set and rely on heavyweight primitives such as distributed ORAM to hide access patterns. As a result, each search typically requires $O(\sqrt{N})$ time. We propose HNSecW, a novel MPC protocol for ANN search that achieves the $O(\log N)$ search time for the first time. We first study the single-query setting. Starting from HNSW, the state-of-the-art ANN algorithm, we redesign its control flow and data structures to achieve fully data-independent execution. To further achieve logarithmic search time, we employ offline reshuffling and partial database duplication. Furthermore, we extend our protocol to support multiple sequential queries by introducing a "double visited" caching structure that eliminates redundant cross-query memory accesses, thereby avoiding per-query online shuffling. In addition, we develop a batch-query protocol that exploits higher parallelism to reduce both round complexity and the circuit's critical path. Our experiments show that HNSecW preserves the high accuracy of plaintext HNSW ($\geq 90\%$ recall) and delivers over a $20\times$ efficiency improvement over prior work on million-scale datasets.

title: Semantic-Aware Deformable Feature Alignment for Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound
summary: Accurate segmentation of thyroid nodules in ultrasound images is essential for clinical diagnosis yet remains challenging due to boundary ambiguity, speckle noise, and complex geometric variability. Existing methods often fail to reconcile global semantic understanding with precise local boundary delineation, leading to errors in irregular cases. To address this, we propose SDFA-Net, a framework built on semantic-aware deformable feature alignment that explicitly decouples the learning of robust global semantics and detailed local geometry. Our approach integrates three main components: a clustered linear context aggregation module for efficient long-range dependency modeling, an affinity-driven token modulation mechanism using dynamic prototypes to suppress background interference, and a cascaded spatially-aligned feature fusion strategy that achieves sub-pixel geometric alignment across multiple resolution stages. By filtering and aligning multi-scale features, SDFA-Net ensures robust fusion that is both semantically meaningful and geometrically accurate. We validate our method through extensive experiments on three public thyroid ultrasound datasets, TN3K, TUCC, and DDTI, where it demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework offers a generalizable solution for precise medical image segmentation in boundary-ambiguous scenarios.

title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
summary: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

title: Honesty Testing of LLMs and AI Agents: A Vision for Software Engineering
summary: Human oversight of large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) agents increasingly depends on their reports. Claims that conflict with a system's own judgments can conceal failures, prevent timely intervention, and contribute to severe harm. Greater autonomy makes faithful reporting increasingly important for maintaining human control. In this vision paper, we propose honesty testing of LLMs and AI agents as a new research area in software engineering. Building on existing honesty evaluations, our goal is to make faithful reporting a software quality requirement that developers can specify, test, and maintain. We define honesty bugs as behavioural defects in which an LLM or AI agent, when required to communicate faithfully, makes an explicit claim that conflicts with its own judgment at the time of reporting. We present an initial framework covering LLM-level testing under controlled inputs and agent-level testing of complete systems. The framework connects these levels to testing workflows and oracle evidence. We identify research directions in benchmarks, model and harness analysis, oracle construction, and lifecycle testing to support effective oversight alongside task correctness.

title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet
summary: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.

title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
summary: A common view regarding even-order nonlinear optical (NLO) effects, such as second-harmonic generation and the bulk photovoltaic effect, is that the breaking of inversion symmetry is necessary. However, this view relies on the assumption that light interacts with materials solely through its electric field. Here, we demonstrate that interference between the electric and magnetic components of the same light field can induce even-order NLO effects even in centrosymmetric materials. Using charge and spin photocurrents as prototypical examples, we present a unified microscopic theory showing how such electric-magnetic dipole interference (EMDI) drives NLO responses in inversion-symmetric crystals. Bilinear in both electric and magnetic fields, these responses scale linearly with light intensity. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, we decompose the EMDI-induced photocurrents into shift-like and injection-like contributions and classify their dependence on crystal symmetry, time-reversal symmetry, and light polarization. Notably, we reveal that these EMDI-induced responses in centrosymmetric materials are weaker than conventional responses in non-centrosymmetric materials roughly by a factor of fine structure constant $α\approx [10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}] $. Nevertheless, they remain well within experimental reach. Our work thus unlocks NLO functionalities in centrosymmetric materials for e.g., materials characterization, photonics and optoelectronics. This is vital given that many functionally importantly materials, such as cubic Si and cubic $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$, possess inversion symmetry.

title: CropReward: A Human-Preference Benchmark and Reward Model for Aesthetic Image Cropping
summary: Aesthetic image cropping (AIC) aims to improve image composition and aesthetic quality by removing extraneous or distracting content. Over the past decade, AIC methods have evolved from specialized vision models to multimodal large language models(MLLMs). Reliable evaluation that reflects human preferences is essential for benchmarking AIC methods and guiding model optimization. However, the current AIC evaluation relies largely on geometry-based metrics such as intersection over union (IoU), as well as image aesthetic assessment(IAA) models. Although inconsistencies with human preferences have long been observed, the robustness and reliability of these evaluation criteria remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, we first construct CropBench, a large-scale benchmark comprising 106,995 human preference pairs for 1,019 images, with each candidate set containing the original image and candidate crops produced by 14 AIC methods. A systematic study on CropBench reveals that the existing criteria, ranging from IoU to off-the-shelf IAA assessment models, only exhibit limited alignment with human preferences. Building upon CropBench, we further propose CropReward, an MLLM-based reward model that evaluates a candidate crop by comparing with the original uncropped image and outputs a score indicating explicit aesthetic improvement or degradation relative to the original. In addition, we employ CropReward to construct CropReward-300k, the largest AIC dataset to date, and further develop CropAlign, a preference-aligned AIC model trained solely with CropReward supervision, without human-annotated crop boxes. Experimental results demonstrate that CropReward aligns with human preferences significantly better than existing criteria. CropAlign also surpasses the state-of-the-art AIC methods, demonstrating the advantage of CropReward in guiding AIC model optimization.

title: ADReasoner: Acoustic-Linguistic Cue-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Explainable Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Speech
summary: Speech-based Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection holds significant promise due to its scalable and non-invasive nature. However, current Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs), similar to conventional AD detection systems, still treat AD detection primarily as a simple categorical classification task. This paradigm provides limited interpretability of predictions, while leaving the inherent expressiveness and reasoning capabilities of SpeechLLMs largely underutilized. In this work, we take the first step toward reframing AD detection as a deep reasoning task via Reinforcement Learning (RL). We propose ADReasoner, an RL-enhanced SpeechLLM designed to generate accurate diagnostic predictions with interpretable rationales grounded in fine-grained acoustic-linguistic cues. To achieve this, we first systematically construct ADCoT-7K, an AD speech reasoning dataset combining real data and our quality-filtered synthetic data, where each instance features Chain-of-Thought (CoT) annotations and detailed captions. Second, observing the weak perception of AD-related acoustic-linguistic cues in current SpeechLLMs, we leverage Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to develop a cue-perception-enhanced foundation model, ADReasoner-Base, thereby improving AD speech understanding. Third, alongside two standard rule-based rewards, we introduce a reasoning reward and a reasoning-label consistency reward into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for RL. Furthermore, a shrinkage mechanism is employed to suppress misleading reasoning signals, while a gating mechanism progressively introduces both rewards to stabilize policy training. Experiments on three AD datasets (Pitt, PROCESS-1, PROCESS-2) demonstrate that ADReasoner outperforms previous state-of-the-art models in both detection performance and explanation quality, advancing AD detection toward interpretable reasoning from speech.

title: From Presence Labels to Bounding Boxes: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Scale Surgical Instrument Localization?
summary: Spatial localization of surgical instruments through bounding-box annotations is a foundational component of surgical scene understanding, supporting detection, tracking, interaction analysis, and grounded vision-language applications. Yet existing annotations often cover selected frames, video subsets, or dataset variants rather than complete procedures. Manual extension is time-consuming and expert-dependent. Additionally, weakly supervised and detector-based pseudo-labels require task-specific training and may be imprecise. In this study, we design a scalable MLLM-based annotation framework that converts surgical frames and existing instrument-presence labels into accurate bounding boxes, and systematically analyze its reliability, cost, and design sensitivity. We instantiate the framework using six MLLMs and a multi-call configuration on laparoscopic cholecystectomy in Cholec80. Using a carefully designed stratification scheme, two annotators independently label 1,000 frames, and an expert surgeon reviews one annotation set to establish the reference. Results show that instrument-set F1 ranges from 88.2 to 92.7,whereas mIoU ranges from 0.180 to 0.735, showing that comparable recognition can conceal large localization differences. A structured multi-stage annotation pipeline achieves 0.784 mIoU, compared with 0.735 for the best single-call baseline and 0.814 human-human agreement. Using the best accuracy pipeline, we create and publicly release a spatial extension of Cholec80 comprising 285,977 bounding boxes across all 184,498 annotated frames from the 80 videos. The annotations and human references are made available on GitHub

title: Higher Reasoning Effort Improves Reference Verifiability and Changes Reasoning Summaries in GPT-5.5
summary: Large language models are increasingly being used in different stages of scientific knowledge production, including the suggestion of references. These models can operate at different levels of reasoning effort and provide summaries of their reasoning processes. This raises two questions: Does increasing reasoning effort improve the verifiability of generated references, and do the resulting reasoning summaries reveal how the model's behavior changes with greater effort? We examined summaries from GPT-5.5 as it generated scholarly references for 1,000 papers under paired low- and high-effort settings. Generated references were matched to external bibliographic records, and reasoning summaries were scored for four predefined features and explored for additional features discovered by GPT-5.5. High effort increased the mean paper-level resolver-verified reference rate from 78.3% to 84.8%, and produced longer reasoning summaries. All four predefined features received higher scores under high effort. The discovered features changed less uniformly: some appeared equally often in both conditions, whereas others were more common under high effort. Within each effort condition, neither feature set showed a consistent increase in verification rates with higher scores.

title: MIS-VQA: An Annotation-Driven Surgical Vision-Language Dataset for Complex Surgical Understanding
summary: Modern surgical AI increasingly requires multimodal understanding rather than isolated perception, yet existing datasets remain largely limited to single-task supervision such as recognition or templated question answering. Current medical VQA resources often rely on synthetic templates, lack natural descriptive supervision, or provide sparse annotations that hinder reasoning about spatial relations and procedural context. We introduce MIS-VQA, a surgical vision-language dataset generated through an annotation-driven pipeline that converts heterogeneous surgical annotations into structured textual scene representations. Using EndoVis18 and CholecT50, we transform phase, instrument, interaction, triplet, and segmentation labels into unified contexts that guide large language models to generate clinically coherent question-answer pairs. MIS-VQA supports four response types-concise and detailed descriptions, perception-level grounding, and multi-step reasoning-enabling hierarchical evaluation from atomic visual grounding to compositional reasoning. To address annotation sparsity, we incorporate confidence-filtered segmentation and cross-annotation consistency checks, enabling spatially grounded supervision at scale. MIS-VQA establishes a unified benchmark for surgical vision-language understanding with spatial supervision and multi-tier reasoning evaluation. To demonstrate its utility, we introduce LLaVA-SurgXpert, a family of surgical vision-language models with visual encoders to analyze how visual representations influence multimodal reasoning. Experiments show consistent improvements over existing surgical VQA baselines while revealing capability gaps between perceptual grounding and higher-level reasoning hidden in prior benchmarks.

title: CORMA: Constraint-Routed Decision Mamba for Generalizable Multi-Constraint Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Offline safe reinforcement learning (RL) learns safety-aware policies from static datasets while satisfying safety constraints during deployment. Motivated by the strong trajectorymodeling capabilities of Transformers, recent Decision Transformer (DT)-based methods formulate offline safe RL as conditional sequence modeling by conditioning action generation on return-to-go (RTG) and cost-to-go (CTG) tokens, thereby enabling adaptation to varying safety budgets. However, existing DT-based methods are developed for single-constraint tasks. For tasks with multiple constraints, generalizing learned policies to unseen combinations of safety budgets remains challenging due to the conflicting requirements imposed by heterogeneous constraints. Moreover, the quadratic complexity of Transformer architectures significantly increases the computational overhead in multi-constraint tasks, as representing additional constraints requires more CTG tokens. Recently, Mamba has emerged as an efficient sequence-modeling backbone, offering linear computational complexity and strong generalization capabilities. In this paper, we propose CORMA, a constraint-routed decision Mamba framework for generalizable multi-constraint offline safe RL. CORMA decomposes policy inference into constraint-aware RTG estimation and adaptive action generation, where constraint-specific experts model feasible RTG distributions and a router-guided product-of-experts mechanism fuses these distributions to provide safety-aware guidance for a Mamba-based action decoder. A three-stage optimization strategy is designed to improve training stability. Extensive experiments on OSRL benchmarks demonstrate that CORMA achieves superior reward-safety trade-offs, reduces inference latency by 37% compared with DT-based methods, and exhibits stronger zero-shot generalization to unseen safety-budget combinations than offline safe RL baselines.

title: kstress: a LAMMPS package for calculating the 2D wavevector-dependent stress tensor and its anisotropy in amorphous solids
summary: The stress tensor resolved in wavevector $\qvec$ and time $t$, $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, gives access to the elastic moduli of amorphous solids as a function of the probed length scale, and to the long-range stress correlations that distinguish an amorphous solid from a liquid. Its evaluation requires the contribution of every interacting pair and therefore an interface to the force loop of the molecular dynamics code. In the current work, we present: i) an optimized implementation of the LAMMPS~\cite{lammps} module for calculating $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, in which trigonometric functions are calculated only for the basic wavevectors and, in addition, all the relevant wavevectors are supplied as an explicit list rather than generated as a full grid, so that only the wavevectors of interest are computed and stored, and ii) a validation protocol for the code illustrated for a two-dimensional polydisperse Lennard-Jones (2DpLJ) glass-forming liquid. Based on these technical achievements we elucidated how the affine moduli for the 2DpLJ model depend on the norm $q$ of the wavevector. In particular, we demonstrate that the longitudinal affine modulus shows a minimum near $q_\text{max}$ corresponding to the main peak of the structure factor. Our data also point to the peaks in the $q$-dependencies of vibrational frequencies well below $q_\text{max}$ for both transverse and longitudinal modes. The potential relevance of this feature to the ``boson peak'' is discussed as well.

title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
summary: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

title: SRA: Selective Residual Adaptation for LLM Reasoning Enhancement
summary: Knowledge distillation transfers reasoning capabilities from large language models to lightweight students. However, distilled small models still struggle with multi-step reasoning. We observe that the distribution divergences between teacher and student models along reasoning paths are highly sparse, and target tokens almost always fall within the student top-$K$ candidate set. Based on this finding, unlike approaches updating student backbones or requiring runtime teacher computation, we propose Selective Residual Adaptation (SRA), a plug-and-play framework that internalizes localized corrections. Concretely, SRA employs a Discrepancy Gate to identify divergence positions alongside a Candidate Residual Adapter for top-$K$ logit calibration to correct the mismatch. Theoretically, we establish error bounds ensuring strict sequence level performance gains. Across mathematical benchmarks on Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 4B, SRA consistently enhances distilled student models, raising average Pass@16 by up to 4.37 percentage points while preserving general capabilities.

title: Testing for Essential Heterogeneity in the Marginal Treatment Effects Model
summary: We propose a test for essential heterogeneity in the marginal treatment effects model without imposing additive separability. On the observed support of the propensity score, no essential heterogeneity implies that the conditional mean of the outcome is affine in the propensity score, and this affine restriction is the sharp testable implication of the null. We implement the test using a projected Gaussian-process statistic that is Neyman-orthogonal to the first-step estimation error, so the multiplier bootstrap avoids re-estimating nuisance parameters. Monte Carlo experiments show accurate size control and good power, and, unlike the fixed-scale integrated conditional moment benchmark, the data-driven median rule retains power as the conditioning set grows in dimension. In an application to the Ugandan ELA programme, the omnibus statistic rejects the null of no essential heterogeneity for aspirations at the midline follow-up.

title: Numerical Construction of Quasi-Periodic Solutions for Nonlinear PDEs: II. Unbounded Perturbation
summary: Many nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in physical models involve unbounded perturbations, where nonlinear terms contain spatial derivatives. Such perturbations can be expressed as compositions of unbounded operators with bounded nonlinear maps. In this paper, we propose alternating numerical schemes for constructing quasi-periodic solutions to this class of PDEs, including the nonlinear acoustic wave (NLAW) equation and the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To render the nonlinear perturbations bounded, we apply inverse differential operators as a preconditioning; this, however, also rescales the linear part by polynomial factors in the spatial mode $n$. Two main difficulties arise. The first is to control the measure of the resulting ``bad'' frequencies, since the bounds on the measures of the excluded frequency sets are enlarged by polynomial factors in $n$; we show that this measure nevertheless remains small. The second concerns resonances involving the perturbed eigenvalues of the linearized operator at large scales. Our key observation is that, when the dispersive frequencies grow polynomially in $n$ with degree greater than one, such resonances cannot occur if the magnitude of the temporal index lies below a threshold proportional to $|n|$ raised to one less than that degree. It therefore suffices to consider the complementary regime, in which the growth induced by the unbounded perturbation can be controlled in terms of the temporal index. At large scales, an additional complication arises: for a given spatial index $n$, all temporal indices in a box may be ``bad''. We show, however, that at each scale there is at most one such spatial index. Consequently, the resulting counting loss is only polynomial and can be absorbed into the exponential-logarithmic threshold, allowing us once again to retain control over the measures of the excluded frequency sets.

title: From Slices to Volumes: Comparing 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Residual Networks for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy-Risk Classification
summary:
Purpose: To compare 2D, 2.5D, and 3D residual networks for pulmonary nodule malignancy-risk classification and evaluate momentum-contrast pretraining, mild augmentation, and exclusion of indeterminate ratings.
  Methods: A retrospectively prepared LIDC-IDRI cohort contained 2,654 nodules labeled benign, indeterminate, or malignant using median radiologist ratings. Patient-disjoint splits comprised 1,876 training, 382 validation, and 396 test nodules. Representations included one axial slice, five neighboring slices, and a local CT volume. Each track evaluated a randomly initialized baseline, momentum-contrast pretraining followed by fine-tuning, and supervised training with mild augmentation. Checkpoints were selected by validation Macro-F1. The 2D experiments used three seeds; 2.5D and 3D results were single-run estimates. A separate binary experiment excluded indeterminate nodules.
  Results: Augmented models achieved test Macro-F1 values of $0.6134\pm0.0075$ for 2D, $0.6537$ for 2.5D, and $0.5403$ for 3D; the 2D uncertainty denotes population standard deviation across seeds. Corresponding accuracies were $0.6128$, $0.6869$, and $0.5455$. Augmentation improved Macro-F1 within every track, whereas the tested pretraining recipes reduced it. Binary Macro-F1 values were $0.8227$, $0.8664$, and $0.7554$, respectively.
  Conclusion: Augmented 2.5D achieved the highest observed performance. Differences in preprocessing, optimization, capacity, and replication limit attribution to dimensionality. Labels reflect radiologist-assessed malignancy risk rather than pathology-confirmed cancer. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/CT-DeepLearning-Team/CT-2D-2.5D-3D-DeepLearning.

title: GeoPrompt: Geometry-Conditioned Prompt Learning for Underwater Open-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation
summary: Open-vocabulary instance segmentation (OVIS) provides a promising solution for marine perception by recognizing and segmenting categories beyond predefined label spaces. Existing OVIS methods usually rely on vision-language alignment, where visual region features are matched with textual category embeddings to recognize both seen and unseen classes. However, this alignment assumption becomes fragile in underwater environments. Color attenuation, scattering, turbidity, and low contrast distort visual appearance, causing region features to deviate from their corresponding semantic concepts. As a result, the similarity between degraded visual features and textual classifiers becomes unreliable, which particularly weakens the recognition of unseen underwater categories that cannot be corrected by category-specific supervision. To address these issues, we propose GeoPrompt, a geometry-conditioned prompt learning framework for underwater open-vocabulary instance segmentation. Our key insight is that geometric structure is more stable than visual appearance in degraded underwater scenes. Specifically, GeoPrompt introduces a geometry-guided visual adaptation module (GVAM) to extract depth-derived structural priors and inject them into multi-scale visual features. It further develops a geometry-conditioned prompt learning (GCPL) that generates geometry-aware textual classifiers from structural representations. These geometry-aware classifiers are integrated with fixed and image-conditioned textual classifiers to improve open-vocabulary semantic alignment. Experiments on the MARIS-OpenIS benchmark show that GeoPrompt achieves state-of-the-art performance and brings consistent improvements on underwater open-vocabulary instance segmentation.

title: Semantic burstiness across principal directions of textual variation
summary: Long-range correlations in written texts extend over scales far beyond local syntax, but their relation to semantic organisation remains incompletely understood. Previous work has linked these correlations to the bursty recurrence of topically relevant words. Here we generalise that construction from individual lexical items to distributed semantic observables. We map a text token by token onto a trajectory of pre-trained word embeddings, use principal component analysis (PCA) to identify text-specific directions of semantic variation, and threshold the projected series to define inter-event times; their coefficients of variation form a component-resolved burstiness spectrum $\{B_k\}$. Across 28 literary and scientific texts and the first 20 components, the originals remain systematically above the geometric inter-event-time baseline and above two complementary controls: a word-shuffled null, which preserves the embedding covariance, the PCA eigensystem and the marginal projected distributions while destroying temporal order, and a fractional-Gaussian-noise surrogate, which preserves the Zipfian frequency structure and matches the detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) exponent of the original rank sequence. With events defined by the upper 5% tail of each projection, the original exceeds both controls in every text-component pair, while the two controls are statistically indistinguishable from each other. Autocorrelation and detrended fluctuation analysis of the semantic projections separate the originals from both controls in the same way. Global rank-level long-range correlations are therefore insufficient to generate the bursty recurrence observed along semantic directions. The results instead support an interpretation in terms of the ordered recurrence of semantically related material.

title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
summary: Extending Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) to humanoid robots requires coordinated whole-body control and diverse demonstrations that are costly to collect in real-world scenarios. Although egocentric human demonstrations provide a complementary source of task experience, differences in visual embodiment and missing robot proprioception complicate transfer to humanoid policies. To address these challenges, we introduce HuGe, a family of Humanoid Generalist VLAs pre-trained on over 2,000 hours of egocentric human and robot data. Specifically, HuGe employs three existing representative VLA architectures to predict latent motion tokens for a pretrained whole-body controller, together with hand-control signals. Based on this, we introduce a three-stage training pipeline that combines egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning. To facilitate transfer across embodiments, we construct pseudo-proprioceptive states through simulation playback during pre-training and modify arm appearance in egocentric observations through re-rendering during downstream fine-tuning. With this pipeline, HuGe achieves the state-of-the-art on simulation benchmark HumanoidArena. Furthermore, real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 indicate that augmenting robot demonstrations with visually adapted egocentric demonstrations significantly increases success on a pick-and-drop task.

title: R2A-Sales: A Policy-Atom-Matched Benchmark for Rule-to-Action Gaps in Goal-Directed Sales Agents
summary: LLM-based sales agents are often evaluated on static policy questions or task success, but deployment asks a sharper question: when a model can state a rule, will it choose compliant, tool-grounded actions under commercial pressure? We introduce R2A-Sales (Rule-to-Action), a policy-atom-matched benchmark for this question. Each item pairs a static probe with a multi-turn sales scenario sharing the same versioned policy atom, facts, evidence, behavioral constraints, and tool contract, so differences cannot be attributed to policy-content mismatch. In the interactive arm, a code-owned ledger verifies committed tool effects and terminal states; unsupported action claims receive no credit. We report static compliance $K$, grounded action compliance $A=\Pr(\text{safe terminal}\land\text{no hard violation}\land\text{non-echo})$, and the matched gap $G=K-A$. The frozen release spans three controlled Chinese-language sales domains, 24 policy atoms, 42 semantic cores, and 2,016 matched pairs. The confirmatory study audits 21,888 runs over 19 cores, covering eight backbones plus four Qwen3-8B prompt treatments (12 configurations). Static compliance is near ceiling $(K=89.9\%\text{--}99.1\%)$, yet eight-backbone action compliance is only $A=3.0\%\text{--}17.3\%$, giving $G=80.4\text{--}92.5$ percentage points. Since $A$ also requires safe termination, $G$ upper-bounds rule-to-action degradation rather than isolating pressure alone. No prompt-only treatment dominates all metrics. R2A-Sales shows that sales-agent reliability must be measured at committed action, not rule recital or task completion alone.

title: Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization: Pre-empting Catastrophic Forgetting via Dynamic Feedback
summary: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of LLMs suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and prevailing mitigation strategies struggle to reconcile the plasticity-stability dilemma. To address this, we propose Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization (ECHO), a closed-loop control framework. By decomposing the KL divergence, we identify output entropy as a dominant observable component of KL variation. This enables us to leverage entropy as a computationally efficient online proxy to monitor forgetting risks in real-time, bypassing expensive reference-model inference. Consequently, ECHO employs an elastic controller that dynamically modulates the gradient weight of replay data via a proportional control law, using deviations from the pre-trained entropic equilibrium as an error signal. Empirical evaluations across 0.6B to 9B parameter architectures demonstrate that ECHO lies on, and in several comparisons extends, the observed plasticity-stability frontier and maintains high operational robustness against varying data mixing ratios.

title: Random-walk scaling without Bernoulli statistics: transport, persistence and resonances in the triangle map
summary: The triangle map is an area-preserving, piecewise-parabolic map of the torus with vanishing Lyapunov exponent. We study the symbolic process $X_n=\pm1$ given by the two halves of the torus, whose partial sums $S_n$ are the transport of the lifted momentum, with an integrator free of accumulated rounding errors and exact computations on polygonal cylinder sets. We prove that the Koopman operator has no non-constant $H^1$ eigenfunctions, that the symbol is not an $H^1$ coboundary, and that runs of equal symbols are uniformly bounded. For generic parameters the walk is normally diffusive and Gaussian, but its diffusion coefficient is not that of a coin: away from the edges of the parameter square it varies between $0.2$ and $14$ times the Bernoulli value, and for a benchmark pair, with $D=3.09\pm0.01$, the excess is produced by the order of the bounded inter-event intervals, not by their distribution. The first-passage exponent is $1/2$ with a non-Bernoulli amplitude, and worst-case Birkhoff averages decay as for a uniquely ergodic system. For $β=0$ the Green-Kubo sum cancels, $D=0$, yet $\mathrm{Var}(S_n)$ keeps growing slowly, sign changes are rare and the correlations of Fourier modes decay as $n^{-0.2}$. We identify the zero-sum words, which become pure twists at $β=0$, as resonances that trap orbits with a computable $1/\ell$ law, set the crossover time $β^{-1/2}$ at small $β$, and, in an asymmetric deformation of the symbol, produce a logarithmic term in the variance whose coefficient we compute exactly. We formulate conjectures on unique ergodicity, mixing, the central limit theorem and the cohomology of the symbol.

title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models
summary: Time Series Foundation Models have demonstrated that pretraining on diverse datasets enables effective transfer to new forecasting tasks. Classical methods like ARIMA, however, remain configured and trained independently for each series, discarding knowledge from previous experiments. Consequently, selecting and training an ARIMA configuration remains challenging and often relies on heuristic approaches based on in-sample goodnessof-fit measures. We propose MetaARIMA, a pretrained configuration policy based on metalearning that brings transfer learning to classical statistical forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level. The policy learns from historical experiments which ARIMA configurations achieve top-quantile performance, and recommends promising candidates for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation. At inference, it selects a diverse set of candidates via maximal marginal relevance and efficiently identifies the final configuration using successive halving. Experiments in a transfer learning setting, training on M4 and evaluating on M1, M3, and Tourism, show that MetaARIMA outperforms AutoARIMA and other classical methods while being more dataefficient. In a comparison with recent zero-shot foundation models, MetaARIMA remains competitive with Chronos2, Moirai2, and TimesFM. The experiments are publicly available at https://github.com/vcerqueira/experiments-metaarima.

title: Cascaded Posterior Sampling With Diffusion Priors for highly Accelerated MRI
summary: Diffusion models are powerful priors for inverse problems, including accelerated MRI. However, modeling the distribution of high-resolution images requires large networks with high computational cost. We propose a posterior sampling framework that uses cascaded diffusion models as multiscale priors. Conditioned on a coarse image, the distribution of fine-scale detail is local and well conditioned, and it can therefore be captured by a small network. Similarly, a small unconditional network is sufficient to represent low-resolution images, and it is used to recover the coarse image from the k-space center. This estimate then conditions the high-resolution prior, which is combined with all measurements to recover the final image. Both priors are trained on images alone, so they apply to any sampling pattern, and data consistency remains linear at every scale. In multi-coil brain MRI, the proposed method improves on the best single-scale diffusion baseline by 4-6 dB in PSNR at 15x acceleration, while each of its separately trained networks is about 10x smaller. The gain grows as the problem becomes more ill-posed, and ablations show that it arises from informative low-resolution conditioning.

title: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents
summary: Tool-using language model agents are usually evaluated by whether they finish the user's task. That metric misses a common failure: an agent can complete the requested work while also taking an unauthorized side-effecting action, such as writing to the wrong object, expanding the scope of the request, or contacting an unintended recipient. We call this failure mode collateral damage (CD). We introduce SABench (Side-effect-Aware Benchmark), a benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks. Each task crosses one of four state structures (independent, dependent, externally reachable, cross-tool) with one of four trap families (ambiguity, mis-targeting, cascade harm, overreach), and each task has a deterministic trace-based oracle for both goal satisfaction and authorization compliance. Across 2,211 model-task pairs from 11 frontier LLMs spanning major commercial and open model families, 15.2% of all runs incur CD, with risk concentrated in ambiguity tasks (38.8% violation rate) while non-ambiguous traps average 8.4% CD. Among goal-satisfied runs, 12.8% still produce unauthorized writes. Cross-tool and dependent states have about twice the CD rate of independent states. CD rates vary by 4.7x across models at comparable goal rates, which suggests that task success alone is a poor proxy for safe tool use. The SABench task corpus is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Phaedrus/sabench; the traces, oracle, code, and analysis pipeline are released at https://github.com/hjj194/sabench-artifact.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Crowd Flow Control Using Dynamic Barriers
summary: Crowd barriers are widely used to regulate pedestrian movement during large public events such as pilgrimages. However, fixed barrier layouts often create unnecessary stopping and local congestion even when they successfully control the overall crowd flow. Finding better barrier configurations is difficult because there is no dataset that provides the best barrier placement for a given crowd scene. We address this challenge by introducing a simulation-driven reinforcement learning framework that learns barrier configurations without requiring labelled training data. Starting from a segmented crowd scene, we construct a realistic simulation environment that reproduces the observed pedestrian distribution. This environment is then used to train a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent that continuously adjusts barrier positions to improve pedestrian movement. Unlike supervised approaches the proposed framework allows the agent to explore barrier configurations that have never been observed in real data. We evaluate the learned policy under unseen numbers of pedestrians. The learned policy consistently outperforms the existing manually designed barrier configuration by reducing pedestrian stops while maintaining effective flow regulation. These results demonstrate that combining computer vision crowd simulation and reinforcement learning provides an effective framework for optimizing crowd control infrastructure.

title: Single-Cycle Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Compressed Continuous Wavelet Features and Deep Neural Networks
